payload.reason: The evidence indicates that the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) melts before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) due to specific climatic and geological conditions during the Last Interglacial (LIG) period, which are not merely for modeling convenience.

claims.text: The Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) contributes to sea level rise before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) during the Last Interglacial (LIG), with GrIS melting first at 125 ka.
The melting of GrIS is driven by continental levering and ocean syphoning, which are significant factors in its earlier contribution to sea level rise compared to AIS.
The two-peak sea level history observed during the LIG is a result of the sequential melting of GrIS followed by AIS, indicating distinct melting dynamics.
